---
title: "Data downloads and caching"
---

The first time you create an atlas, `iblatlas` downloads its data, which is about 40 MB at the
default 25 µm resolution. The extra datasets download only when you load them, and are larger.

```python
ba = AllenAtlas()   # first call: downloads about 40 MB. Later calls: read from cache.
```

The download happens once per resolution and is cached on disk. Subsequent calls are cheap.

| Data | Approximate size |
|---|---|
| Atlas at 25 µm (default) | 40 MB |
| Gene expression (AGEA) | 2.6 GB |
| MERFISH | 630 MB |
| Depths | 350 MB |
| Lipids | 105 MB |
| Flat maps | 30 MB |

## Where the data goes

The cache directory is derived from ONE's `CACHE_DIR` parameter by
`BrainAtlas._get_cache_dir`, which appends a fixed subpath:

```
<ONE CACHE_DIR>/histology/ATLAS/Needles/Allen
```

`CACHE_DIR` defaults to `~/Downloads/ONE/openalyx.internationalbrainlab.org`.

Note that `Needles` appears in the path regardless of which atlas you instantiate — it is part
of the historical layout, not a statement about the scaling in use. See
[Atlas spaces and transforms](atlas-spaces.qmd).

## Files downloaded on demand

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `annotation_<res_um>.nrrd` | Region **indices** (not ids) per voxel, uint16, at the given isometric spacing |
| `average_template_<res_um>.nrrd` | The template image volume |
| `annotation_<res_um>_lut_<LUT_VERSION>.npz` | Lookup table |
| `swansonpaths.json` | Vectorised Swanson flat map paths |
| `swanson2allen.npz` | — |
| `<flatmap_name>_<res_um>.nrrd` | — |
| `connectivity/allen_mouse_regionalized_connectivity.pqt` | Oh / Knox mesoscale connectivity, regionalized onto 291 Allen summary structures |
| `connectivity/allen_mouse_hierarchy_scores.pqt` | Harris cortico-thalamic hierarchy scores, 61 cortical and thalamic areas |

Note the annotation volumes store the region **index** — the position in the flattened
structure tree — not the Allen id. See
[The brain region hierarchy](brain-region-hierarchy.qmd).

## Two remote sources

- **The Allen Institute**, over HTTP, for the atlas volumes themselves
  (`_download_atlas_allen`). The data is the Allen Mouse Brain Atlas (2015) with the 2017
  region annotations.
- **The `ibl-brain-wide-map-public` S3 bucket**, declared as `S3_BUCKET_IBL`, for the
  IBL-repackaged resources — the flat maps, the genomics volumes, the connectivity tables and
  the streamlines described in
  [External data in the common space](external-data-in-the-common-space.qmd).

## Changing where files are saved

`_get_cache_dir` reads the cache location from ONE, the IBL data-access package that
`iblatlas` installs and uses for downloading. ONE needs no setup: with its default settings the
cache is `~/Downloads/ONE/openalyx.internationalbrainlab.org`, and no account, login or
credentials are involved. The S3 bucket is read without credentials too.

To save files somewhere else, set the ONE cache directory once, before first use:

```python
from one.params import setup

setup(silent=True, cache_dir='/path/to/cache')
```

The new location starts empty, so the next load downloads the data again, and the copy in your
Downloads folder is left unused. To avoid downloading again, move or copy the existing
`histology` folder into the new cache directory so that
`<new cache dir>/histology/ATLAS/Needles/Allen/` holds the files. `iblatlas` only checks that each
file exists at that path, so files moved without that folder structure are not found.

## Practical consequences

- **Do not instantiate an atlas in a tight loop.** Build one and pass it in. Most functions
  that need one accept a `brain_atlas` or `br` argument for exactly this reason.
- **Resolution costs space.** The 10 µm volume is substantially larger than the 25 µm default;
  take the default unless you need the detail.
